newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, swaps up but off high.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, swaps up but off high.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in late trading on Tuesday, dealers said.
They said swap premiums were off highs but remained well bid on fears that the Indonesian central bank might control swap transactions, emulating the Malaysian move.
Malaysia's Bank Negara said on Sunday that local banks will have to limit their non-trade related currency swaps to $2.0 million with each overseas customer from Monday.
Although many operators were sceptical of a similar move in Indonesia, swaps rose before easing in the afternoon.
Six-month swap increased to 135 points before settling at 128/135 points. Three-month swap was last at 63/67, down from previous high of 70.0 points.
While longer-term swaps were determined by the swap control issue, short-term premiums were directed by liquidity.
However, overnight money fell to 14.5 percent from an early high of 28.0 percent on initial liquidity tightening fears.
Overnight swap was 1.0/1.2 and tom/next at 0.7/0.8.
Dealers said the central bank was likely to maintain its tight grip on the money market for this week before returning to its initial policy of bringing interest rates lower.
The central bank was embarking on lower a interest rate environment before the currency turmoil in Thailand spread to the region and forced Bank Indonesia to alter its short-term monetary policy.
Dealers said initial downward pressure on the dollar seemed to ease in the afternoon after liquidity slowly turned around.
But one U.S. bank dealer said sustained dollar purchase by local operators was slowing the dollar correction.
"We received plenty of offshore dollar selling. But the dollar remains stable because of strong domestic buying."
Another dealer said he did not believe the central bank would impose swap controls in Indonesia.
"It would mean a setback in its liberalisation effort," the dealer said, adding that the central bank would consider such a move if there was an emergency.
Dealers said the rupiah was still hovering within the range of 2,555 and 2,610, indicated by the central bank as normal.
They said sentiment was improving after the Thai baht was on the way to recovery as the country seemed to be moving closer to approving the IMF recovery package.
Spot rupiah was at 2,598/2,600 at 0940 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,600/05. Tomorrow and today rupiah ended at 2,597/99 and 2,597/98, respectively.

Dealers said liquidity would remain the focus on Wednesday as operators had to rely fully on the interbank market as the central bank had stopped the auction of short-term papers (SBPUs) and did not offer repo on central bank certificates.
Operators were concerned over a possible tighter condition on Wednesday if the central bank did not allow roll-overs of some 200 billion rupiah maturing repo papers from last week.
One-month swap was at 21.0/24.0, two at 43.0/52.0, three at 63.0/67.0 and six at 128.0/135.0 points.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 but lowered the conversion band to 2,576/2,624 on Tuesday from 2,580/2,628 on Monday. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
